title: Local Hilbert--Samuel presentations and their admissible transforms
statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, locally closed in a smooth scheme $Z$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $h_x(n)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x^{n+1})$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length], $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{i=0}^n f(i)$, and $H_X(x)=\Lambda^{\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbf Q}\kappa(x)}h_x$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree] [def-weil-residue-field]. Then $H_X$ has finite image locally, is upper semicontinuous for lexicographic order, and cannot increase under a blowup with smooth center on which $H_X$ is locally constant. There is no infinite strictly decreasing sequence of its values along admissible blowups of a fixed initial finite-dimensional $X$.

At each $a\in X$, after restriction and an etale neighbourhood [def-weil-etale-morphism], there are a smooth closed $N\hookrightarrow Z$, a coherent ideal $I\subset\mathcal O_N$ [pqf-def-coherent], and $b\ge1$, such that $\{x\in N:\operatorname{ord}_x I\ge b\}$ is the local $H_X(a)$ equality stratum. Here $\operatorname{ord}_x I=\sup\{q:I_x\subset\mathfrak m_x^q\}$, allowing infinity for zero. A presentation means more than equality of these sets: along every finite admissible test sequence, its cosupport is exactly the locus retaining that Hilbert--Samuel level (with the level summed after a line product).

The test operations are smooth blowups with centers in that stratum having normal crossings with the ordered exceptional divisors, products with an affine line, and blowups of intersections of two exceptional divisors. Normal crossings means that the center is a coordinate subspace in an etale coordinate system in which boundary components are distinct coordinate hyperplanes. For an admissible blowup, $X$ and $N$ take scheme-theoretic strict transform and $I$ takes total transform divided by the $b$th power of the new exceptional ideal [def-nagata-global-blowup] [def-nagata-strict-transform]. For the other two operations take ordinary pullbacks of $X,N,I$; a line product appends the zero section as last boundary component. Blowups retain the ordered strict transforms of boundary components and append the new exceptional divisor. The ordered boundary of a test sequence is empty at the stage where the presentation is taken and consists only of the divisors created by the operations of that sequence (new exceptional divisors and line zero sections); exceptional divisors created before that stage are recorded history data and are not used as test boundary. Presentations are equivalent when all these test sequences agree.

At a singular point of $X$, use a minimal smooth local envelope (the ambient cotangent space maps isomorphically to that of $X$); a presentation is then etale-locally equivalent to one on the whole envelope ($N=Z$) whose ideal has order exactly its positive marking $b$ throughout cosupport. Presentations at regular points still exist; no finite maximal-order assertion is made for the zero ideal on a codimension-zero regular germ. Up to common etale comparison, the class of a presentation at a specified Hilbert--Samuel level is independent of the chosen minimal envelope and of its coefficient data. Along admissible histories it depends only on the intrinsic transformed scheme, the retained level and the ordered earlier center ideals, with the induced boundary data. It commutes with restriction and local smooth pullback: for a smooth map of relative dimension $r$ the level $H$ is replaced by $\Lambda^r H$, so equality strata and test conditions pull back. This does not assert that the numerical value of $H$ is invariant under a positive-dimensional smooth map. Emptying the cosupport of a presentation of a maximum stratum removes that maximum from the strict transform. These assertions concern presentations and their transforms, not a completed resolution tower.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.93--94; detailed input WANTED: BMT arXiv:0905.3580 sections 6.1--6.3 and BM marked presentations. No Stacks tag states this presentation theorem.

proof.text: Work in an affine etale chart of the smooth ambient. By [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control], each $H_X(x)(n)$ is a finite Taylor-module fibre dimension and is the count of missing monomials in its diagram. The diagrams take finitely many values locally, so $H_X$ does also. Its possible values in any fixed number of ambient variables satisfy the descending-chain condition. The same ambient variable bound works along blowups, whose charts have the same dimension; thus this condition also applies to values encountered later, rather than just to the initial finite image.

On an affine chart, the coordinate ring is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] (a field has only the ideals zero and one). A finite Taylor module has a finite presentation since its relation module is a submodule of a finite free module [lem-trf-noetherian-submodule-finitely-presented]. For a matrix with $v$ target rows, fibre dimension at least $c$ means that all $(v-c+1)$-minors vanish: this follows by row reduction over the residue field. Thus each coordinate $H_X(\cdot)(n)$ is upper semicontinuous. On the finite set of local sequence values from [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control], choose $n_1$ at least the first index at which any two of these values differ. Intersect the neighbourhoods where each coordinate $n\le n_1$ is at most its value at $a$. If $H_X(x)\ne H_X(a)$ there, they first differ at some $n\le n_1$, where $H_X(x)(n)<H_X(a)(n)$; so the neighbourhood has $H_X(x)\le H_X(a)$ lexicographically. Applying this at each point of a strict lower-level set proves that every lexicographic upper-level set is closed.

source.place: BM 1997, Remarks 9.1, Theorem 9.2 and Lemma 9.3; finite-matrix argument written out.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-data] after the preceding shrinking. It gives a smooth $N$, regular coefficients $c_{i\gamma}$ and positive weights $m_{i\gamma}=d_i-|\gamma|$ for $|\gamma|<d_i$. Choose a positive common multiple $b$ of these finitely many weights and set $I=\sum_{i,\gamma}(c_{i\gamma}^{\,b/m_{i\gamma}})$ on $N$; if the list is empty take $b=1$ and $I=0$. In a smooth Taylor ring the order of a nonzero product is the sum of its orders, since its first nonzero homogeneous terms multiply to a nonzero polynomial. Consequently $\operatorname{ord} I\ge b$ is exactly the set of all the coefficient inequalities. The initial-stratum assertion of [lem-trf-formal-coefficient-transform-criterion] identifies this set with the $H_X(a)$ equality locus. Coherence of this finite generated ideal and of its finite free relation modules follows from [lem-trf-noetherian-submodule-finitely-presented]. This is a construction of the ideal, not a choice from a bare existence theorem.

source.place: BM 1997, Theorems 9.4 and 9.6; BMT 6.2, combining marked functions by common powers.

proof.text: Take a smooth center contained in this equality locus and in normal crossings with the boundary. The normal coordinates for its inclusion in the smooth ambient are supplied by [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates]. The formulas of [lem-trf-formal-coefficient-transform-criterion] give $c'_{i\gamma}=e^{-m_{i\gamma}}\sigma^*c_{i\gamma}$ on the strict transform of $N$. Taking the powers used above gives $(c'_{i\gamma})^{b/m_{i\gamma}}=e^{-b}\sigma^*(c_{i\gamma}^{b/m_{i\gamma}})$; hence the transformed coefficient ideal is precisely the controlled transform of $I$. The same theorem gives $H_{X'}(a')\le H_X(a)$ and characterizes equality by these coefficient inequalities, with the five division/Jacobian conditions retained at equality points. Away from the center the blowup is an isomorphism by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], and the strict transform restricts to the original scheme by [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-over-complement]. Shrinking around any point of a locally $H$-constant center proves the stated nonincrease for all such blowups.

source.place: BM 1997, Theorems 7.20 and 9.4; Stacks 0FUE for smooth-pair coordinates.

proof.text: The other formulas of [lem-trf-formal-coefficient-transform-criterion] use ordinary pullback for an exceptional intersection blowup; $X$ is then a total transform, not an arbitrarily stipulated strict transform. For a line product the Taylor count in [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control] replaces $H$ by $\Lambda H$. Adjoin the horizontal zero section to the ordered boundary. Induct on the length of a test sequence, carrying also the claim that every boundary component is transverse to the current $N$ (its equation is a coordinate of $N$ in the coordinates $(W,Z)$): the boundary is empty at length zero; an admissible center lies in the cosupport, hence in $N$, so in each chart meeting the strict transform of $N$ the exceptional equation and the strict transforms of earlier boundary coordinates are $W$-coordinates; a line zero section and the exceptional divisor of a blowup of two such boundary hyperplanes are again given by $W$-coordinates. This is the transversality hypothesis of the exceptional-intersection formula. For length zero the initial equality criterion was proved in step 3. For an admissible blowup apply step 4 and retain the division data at equality points; for the other two operations use the just cited formulas. Thus at each stage the two cosupports coincide and allow exactly the same next smooth center. This proves equality of all test sequences, with the specified exceptional ordering.

First choose a minimal smooth envelope by [lem-trf-smooth-embedding-etale-comparison], and perform step 3 there. At a singular point its Taylor ideal is nonzero, so the construction uses at least one essential transverse variable: otherwise the diagram would be empty and the local scheme would be the smooth envelope. The smooth pair has etale transverse retraction coordinates by the same comparison node. Apply [lem-trf-marked-ideal-transverse-suspension] to $(N,I,b)$ in those coordinates. Its explicit ideal $J=(z_1^b,\ldots,z_r^b)+p^*I$ has the same test sequences, is on the whole envelope, and has order exactly $b$ along cosupport since $r\ge1$. For a regular codimension-zero germ take $N=Z$, $I=0$, $b=1$; the equality/test description still holds, while order is infinite. This explains the necessary singular-point restriction on the maximal-order clause.

source.place: BMT 6.2, minimal embedding and maximal-order paragraph; explicit regular-germ exception.

proof.text: A smooth morphism is locally etale over an affine-space projection by [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form]. The Taylor-module identities of [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control] are invariant under that etale localization, and adjoining $r$ free variables gives $H_Y=\Lambda^rH_X$ on a piece of relative dimension $r$. For two different sequences the first nonzero coefficient of their difference is also the first nonzero coefficient of its partial sum, with the same sign. Thus $\Lambda^r$ preserves and reflects lexicographic inequalities and equality. Pull back the coefficient construction; its test-transform identities remain the identities in step 4, now in the pulled-back coordinates. Therefore it is a presentation of the summed level. This is a local assertion on each relative-dimension piece; it does not synchronize the numerical maxima of different pieces.

source.place: BMT 6.3, line-product formula and smooth functoriality; BM 1997, Definition 6.2.

proof.text: Any two coefficient constructions in a fixed envelope present the same intrinsic retaining-level test data by step 5; hence their sequences agree, which is exactly equivalence. Two minimal envelopes have a common etale comparison identifying their closed copies of $X$ by [lem-trf-smooth-embedding-etale-comparison]. On that comparison apply the preceding observation. This identifies classes, not a uniquely chosen coefficient ideal. The comparisons pull back every specified earlier center ideal. Repeating the retaining-level criterion of step 5 after each center therefore also identifies the induced ordered boundary and subsequent transformed presentations. Restriction is obtained by applying the very same formulas in a smaller open neighbourhood. This proves the claimed intrinsic dependence for these admissible histories, without a new assertion about arbitrary ambient histories.

Suppose the presentation is of the maximum level $H_0$ and an admissible sequence empties its cosupport. At each preceding stage the equality criterion of step 5 says that every point with value $H_0$ is in that cosupport, while nonincrease in step 4 rules out values above $H_0$. Thus no final point has value $H_0$. The diagram descending-chain condition of [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control] applies at every stage in the same ambient dimension; it rules out infinitely many strict drops. The ambient and strict transform remain smooth and reduced, respectively, by [lem-trf-smooth-center-blowup-geometry], after restriction to finite-type separated smooth charts. Induction therefore reapplies the construction at every admissible history. No resolution engine is invoked to turn this conditional disappearance statement into an assertion of a completed tower.
